guestCategory: UGA parents on game and campus weekends

brand.promise: Eleven acres between you and noise.
brand.promiseMeaning: The quiet is the product. Every touchpoint protects it or gets out of its way.
brand.personality: A calm Georgia neighbor who waves from the porch, answers fast, and then leaves you be.
brand.voice: Short, warm and plain. Specifics over adjectives: acres, minutes, bird names. Never pushy, never loud.

persona.name: Denise Whitfield
persona.snapshot: 52, operations director from Alpharetta. Married to Mark. Daughter is a junior at UGA.
persona.why: To be close to her daughter and the Dawgs without paying Athens game-day rates or sleeping somewhere loud.

experienceLine: Denise leaves the game-day noise at the gate, sleeps like she's at home, and books next season before she gets back to Alpharetta.

beats.title: Confirmation
beats.headline: Confirm fast, answer the stairs question before she asks
beats.scene: Denise taps Request to Book at 9:40 pm, half expecting silence until morning. Twelve minutes later her phone lights up with a reply that uses her name and answers the one thing she hadn't asked yet.
beats.feelsBefore: Unsure about a listing with 2 reviews.
beats.feelsAfter: Relieved. A real person is on the other end.
beats.promiseProof: Quiet starts with no worry. A fast, plain reply removes the first source of noise: doubt.
beats.script:
Hi Denise, you're all set for Oct 17 to 19. It's about 25 minutes to Sanford Stadium. On game day, take Hwy 129 in and give yourself extra time.
One honest note: there are stairs up to the studio. We'll leave a luggage cart at the bottom for the cooler and bags.
We live on the property but on the far side of the meadow. You'll have the patio and the quiet to yourselves.
beats.risk: the reply is a long template, or the stairs are a surprise on arrival.

beats.title: Personalization
beats.headline: One question, then a game-day guide made for her weekend
beats.scene: A week out, Denise gets one short question: early riser or night owl, and is your student joining you? Her answer shapes the guide that arrives two days later.
beats.feelsBefore: Busy, planning around the game schedule.
beats.feelsAfter: Looked after. The plan is already half made.
beats.promiseProof: Personal, but not chatty. One question, then everything she needs in one place, so she doesn't have to research.
beats.script:
Game Day from Songbird Acres
• Leave by 9:30 for a noon kickoff and book campus parking ahead.
• Breakfast: our favorite spot in downtown Jefferson opens early.
• Groceries: the nearest store is about 10 minutes away.
• Back by dark? The patio lights come on at sunset.
beats.risk: it reads like a brochure, or it pushes paid extras she didn't ask for.

beats.title: Smooth check-in
beats.headline: Gate, parking, keypad: three steps, no calls
beats.scene: The gravel crunches, then stops. A small sign says 'Guests park here' next to the stairs. The keypad works on the first try. Mark carries the cooler up on the cart. Inside, it is completely quiet.
beats.feelsBefore: Tired from the drive and Athens traffic.
beats.feelsAfter: Calm the second the car door shuts.
beats.promiseProof: No knocking, no meeting, no fumbling. The arrival itself is quiet.
beats.script: Morning Denise. Your code is 4417. Park on the gravel pad by the stairs (sign says Guests). The cart is at the bottom of the steps. Text this number if anything is off. We'll stay out of your way.
beats.risk: the code fails, parking is unclear, or a host walks over to say hello on the first evening.

beats.title: Welcome token
beats.headline: Pecans, a 'Go Dawgs' card and binoculars by the window
beats.scene: On the counter: a jar of pecans from the trees outside, a handwritten card in red ink, and a pair of binoculars on the windowsill with a card naming the six birds most seen from the patio.
beats.feelsAfter: Delighted. This place was set up for her.
beats.promiseProof: The gift is the land itself: pecans from the property, birds from the meadow. It points her outside, into the quiet.
beats.script: Denise and Mark, welcome. The pecans are from the trees you passed on the way in. The cardinals show up around 7 am. Go Dawgs. (Quietly.)
beats.risk: it becomes a branded tchotchke or a pile of plastic-wrapped snacks.

beats.title: Communicate
beats.headline: One check-in message, then a 10-minute fix when Wi-Fi dips
beats.scene: Denise needs to send one work email before the game. The Wi-Fi drops. She texts the host, expecting to wait. Nine minutes later: a reset tip that works, plus a backup hotspot left at the door.
beats.feelsBefore: Annoyed. The one thing she needed failed.
beats.feelsAfter: Impressed. It was handled faster than at home.
beats.promiseProof: A problem is noise. Fixing it fast and without fuss puts the quiet back.
beats.script: So sorry, Denise. Unplug the white box under the TV for 30 seconds, it's back in 2 minutes. I've also left a hotspot at the bottom of the stairs (password on the back) so you're covered for the weekend.
beats.risk: the reply takes hours, blames the rural internet, or turns into a long apology.

beats.title: Quality
beats.headline: Spotless, hotel-made bed, and everything labeled
beats.scene: The king bed is made tight with white linens. Kitchen drawers have small labels. The house book is one page, not twenty. Nothing hums, rattles or beeps.
beats.feelsBefore: Watchful. Is it as clean as the photos?
beats.feelsAfter: At ease. Nothing to fix, nothing to figure out.
beats.promiseProof: Clean and working means no small irritations. Labels mean no questions. The house stays silent.
beats.script:
Wi-Fi: SongbirdAcres / meadow2026
Thermostat: by the bedroom door
Quiet hours are every hour. Enjoy them.
Checkout: 11 am, just 3 things (on the back).
beats.risk: dust, hair, a musty smell, a beeping smoke alarm, or a 20-page manual.

beats.title: Make it simple
beats.headline: Three tasks and a late checkout after night games
beats.scene: Sunday after a night game, Denise wakes at 9 to a message: checkout is moved to 1 pm, no charge. She has coffee on the patio, watches two deer cross the meadow, loads the dishwasher, and leaves.
beats.feelsAfter: Unhurried. The weekend ends on the best note.
beats.promiseProof: An unhurried ending is part of the quiet. Short list, late exit, no chore chart.
beats.script: Late night? Take your time. Checkout is 1 pm today, no charge. Just: dishes in the dishwasher, towels in the tub, door locks itself. Safe drive home.
beats.risk: a long chore list, a 10 am checkout after a night game, or a cleaner arriving early.
beats.owner: Scheduled message, host decides the late checkout
beats.cost: $0 when the next night is empty

beats.title: Offer support
beats.headline: A route home and a 'did you forget anything?' check
beats.scene: On the drive home, Denise gets a short text: the cleaner found her daughter's UGA hoodie. It's in the mail tomorrow.
beats.promiseProof: Neighborly means you look out for people, then step back. One message, a solved problem, no ask.
beats.script: Hi Denise, found a red UGA hoodie on the sofa. We'll mail it tomorrow to the address on your booking unless you'd like it held for your next trip.
beats.risk: the message includes a review ask or a sales pitch.

beats.title: Say thanks
beats.headline: A real thank-you that names something from her stay
beats.scene: Monday at lunch, Denise reads a message that mentions the deer she told the host about and the Dawgs' win. It doesn't ask for anything.
beats.promiseProof: Honest and unhurried. Thanks comes on its own, not as a setup for a request.
beats.script: Denise, thank you for staying with us. Glad the deer showed up for your coffee, and what a win Saturday. The meadow will be here whenever you need it.
beats.risk: it is a generic template or bundles in the review request.
beats.owner: Claude drafts, host personalizes one line

beats.title: Request review
beats.headline: Ask once, say why it matters for a new place
beats.scene: Three days later, one short message explains that Songbird Acres is new and that a few honest words help other UGA parents find a quiet place.
beats.feelsAfter: Happy to help. She writes it that evening.
beats.promiseProof: Honest: the ask says exactly why. Quiet: it is asked once, never chased.
beats.script: One small favor: we're new, and other UGA parents read reviews closely. If you have a minute, a few honest words about the quiet and the drive in would help them find us. Thank you either way.
beats.risk: it asks for 5 stars, sends reminders, or offers anything in return for a review.

beats.title: Network
beats.headline: Keep in touch on her terms, and give her a link to share
beats.when: In the thank-you, then twice a year
beats.scene: Denise is in the UGA parents Facebook group when someone asks for 'somewhere quiet that isn't $500 a night.' She pastes the Songbird Acres link the hosts gave her.
beats.feelsAfter: Helpful. She's the one with the good tip.
beats.promiseProof: Neighborly: a small list of past guests who hear from you rarely, and only with something useful.
beats.script: If you'd like first pick of next season's game weekends, reply 'yes' and we'll send one note when the schedule is out. That's it, no newsletters.
beats.risk: she gets added to a weekly email list or tagged in posts without asking.

beats.title: Incentivize
beats.headline: First pick of game weekends, not a discount
beats.when: The day the UGA schedule is released
beats.scene: In February the schedule drops. Before Athens hotels reprice, Denise gets one message offering her first pick of three home-game weekends. She books two.
beats.promiseProof: The reward is access, not a coupon. It protects margin and makes returning feel like coming home.
beats.script: The 2027 schedule is out. Before we open the calendar to everyone, you get first pick: Sept 11, Oct 2 or Nov 13. Reply with a date and it's yours.
beats.risk: it becomes a blanket discount, or it's sent to everyone at once.
touchpoints: Text or email to past guests

preStay.how: Reply within the hour. Name the stairs, the drive time and where the hosts live.
Send one photo of the meadow at dusk with the 7-day message.
Ask one question: early riser or night owl, and is your student joining?
Code, parking pad and cart in one text at 10 am arrival day.
Skip paid partnerships. Name two local places you'd send a friend instead.
Game-day route and timing, campus parking, breakfast in Jefferson.
Stairs, shared grounds, no fires, and that it's genuinely quiet.

stay.how: Keypad, signed parking, 3-task checkout, late checkout after night games.
Property pecans, handwritten card, binoculars and a bird card.
One page. No tour, because no meeting is part of the promise.
Small labels on drawers, thermostat and Wi-Fi.
Text replies inside 15 minutes, 7 am to 10 pm. Backup hotspot ready.
Checklist with photo proof after each turnover. Smell test before every arrival.
Test Wi-Fi, keypad battery and smoke alarms at every turnover.

afterStay.how: Next day, one personal line, no ask.
Offer first pick of game weekends. Reply 'yes' to opt in.
A small past-guest list in your phone or PMS. Two messages a year.
Day 3, once, with the honest reason why.
Give her the link to share when parents ask for quiet places.
Early access to game weekends instead of a discount.
Schedule release (Feb) and graduation booking window (Jan).

buildList.item: Write the 8 message scripts once with Claude and save them as scheduled messages
Past-guest list with an opt-in column
Binoculars and a printed bird card
Luggage cart at the foot of the stairs

never: Walk over to say hello. Wave from a distance if you cross paths.
Send more than one message on any day of the stay unless she writes first.
Ask for 5 stars or offer anything in exchange for a review.
Use exclamation marks, 'cozy', 'nestled' or 'oasis' in any message.
Run a leaf blower, mower or any loud work while guests are on site.
Discount to win a rebooking. Offer first access instead.
measures: Reply time to first inquiry (goal: under 1 hour)
Reviews that mention 'quiet', 'peaceful' or 'host' (goal: most of them)
Review rate after the day-3 ask (goal: 60%+)
Past guests who opt in for first pick (goal: 1 in 2)
footer: Sample storyboard. The brand core was written for this demo from the public listing; run the brand step first for a real one. Denise is a composite guest from the Guest Intelligence Report sample, not a real person. Costs are rough estimates.
